question: What is the medical term often used for andropause?
explanation: Andropause is medically referred to as late-onset hypogonadism because testosterone production gradually decreases as men age. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T8#GNS121_U4_T8_h1)

question: How does andropause mostly differ from female menopause?

options.A: Hormone levels drop to zero within a few months
options.B: Symptoms only appear in men over the age of eighty
options.C: Testosterone decline happens very slowly over years
options.D: Reproductive capacity ends abruptly in men

explanation: Male hormone decline is a gradual process that spans decades, whereas female menopause involves a clear stop in menstruation and ovulation. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T8#GNS121_U4_T8_h1)

question: Which cells in the testes produce testosterone?
explanation: Leydig cells in the testes make and release testosterone when stimulated by luteinizing hormone. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T8#GNS121_U4_T8_h2)

question: Why does an increase in sex hormone-binding globulin lower testosterone effectiveness?

options.A: It converts active testosterone directly into estrogen
options.B: It destroys the hormone molecules in the liver
options.C: It blocks the pituitary gland from releasing luteinizing hormone
options.D: It binds free testosterone and prevents tissue uptake

explanation: Sex hormone-binding globulin attaches to circulating testosterone, leaving very little free hormone available to work on body tissues. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T8#GNS121_U4_T8_h2)

question: What is a common physical sign of dropping testosterone levels in older men?

options.B: Excessive daily red blood cell production
options.D: Loss of muscle mass and strength

explanation: Testosterone helps build muscle, so lower levels lead to a noticeable drop in muscle mass and overall physical strength. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T8#GNS121_U4_T8_h3)

question: A patient with andropause feels down and irritable. What type of symptoms are these?
explanation: Mood changes like depression, irritability, and trouble concentrating are psychological and emotional signs of low testosterone. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T8#GNS121_U4_T8_h3)

question: At what time of day should blood be drawn to accurately measure testosterone?
explanation: Testosterone levels are highest in the early morning, making that the best time to draw blood for an accurate baseline. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T8#GNS121_U4_T8_h4)

question: Why do clinicians check for thyroid issues during an andropause evaluation?

options.A: Thyroid hormones neutralize replacement testosterone entirely
options.B: Thyroid tests confirm the exact age of the patient
options.C: Other endocrine disorders can cause identical symptoms
options.D: Low testosterone always damages the thyroid gland first

explanation: Conditions like hypothyroidism share many signs with andropause, so testing helps rule them out for an accurate diagnosis. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T8#GNS121_U4_T8_h4)

question: What lab value must nurses monitor closely in patients on testosterone replacement therapy?
explanation: Testosterone boosts red blood cell production, which can raise hemoglobin and hematocrit to unsafe levels if left unmonitored. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T8#GNS121_U4_T8_h5)

question: Why are regular prostate checks necessary for men receiving testosterone therapy?

options.A: Testosterone can stimulate growth in existing prostate conditions
options.B: Prostate tissue shrinks rapidly with added hormones
options.C: Prostate fluid is required to activate the medication
options.D: It prevents urinary tract infections caused by catheters

explanation: Adding testosterone can speed up the growth of prostate cancer or worsen benign prostatic hyperplasia, requiring careful monitoring. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T8#GNS121_U4_T8_h5)

question: Which type of exercise helps manage the physical changes of andropause?
explanation: Resistance or strength training helps fight the loss of muscle mass and supports bone density when testosterone declines. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T8#GNS121_U4_T8_h6)

question: What is the main goal of lifestyle counseling for a patient with andropause?

options.A: To support symptom management without relying solely on drugs
options.B: To guarantee a permanent return of youth hormone levels
options.C: To completely reverse the natural aging process
options.D: To eliminate the need for any future medical evaluations

explanation: Diet and exercise changes help patients manage symptoms and feel better alongside or instead of medication. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T8#GNS121_U4_T8_h6)
